concepts.name: Compressed Sensing
concepts.short_description: Recovering sparse signals from far fewer measurements than Nyquist; RIP, basis pursuit, L1 minimization.

concepts.name: Measure Theory
concepts.short_description: Rigorous foundation for integration and probability; sigma-algebras, Lebesgue measure, convergence theorems.

concepts.name: Symbiosis
concepts.short_description: Long-term interspecies interaction with mutual benefit; mutualism, endosymbiosis, holobiont theory.

defining_structures: k-sparse vector x in R^n (or sparse in a dictionary Psi)
measurement matrix A (m x n, m << n)
decoder: L1 minimisation / basis pursuit / greedy pursuit
invariants: restricted isometry: ||A x|| ~ ||x|| for all k-sparse x
null space property: no k-sparse-dominated vector in ker A
conserved_quantities: energy of sparse vectors (approximately, under RIP)
failure_modes: abrupt phase transition: recovery collapses once k/m crosses a curve
signal not sparse in the assumed basis
dynamics: iterative thresholding converges to a sparse fixed point
sharp success/failure transition as m or k varies
locality: sparsity is locality in coefficient index, not in space
memory: a small set of measurements stores the whole sparse signal
identity: the support set identifies the signal
two signals are equivalent iff they differ by an element of ker A
reproduction: none intrinsic; a measurement row can be copied or transferred
information: about k log(n/k) measurements suffice for the support
constraint: incoherence between sensing and sparsity bases

invariants: absolute continuity nu << mu is preserved under restriction
integral is invariant under modification on null sets
transformations: conditional expectation = projection onto a sub-sigma-algebra
conserved_quantities: mass of each measurable set under measure-preserving maps
failure_modes: escape of mass to infinity (failure of tightness / domination)
limits and integrals not commuting without monotonicity or domination
singular measures invisible to a density
memory: filtration F_t: the growing sigma-algebra of what has been observed
identity: equality almost everywhere: objects differing on a null set are the same
information: a sigma-algebra is the information: which events can be distinguished
constraint: only measurable events can be acted on

defining_structures: host and symbiont lineages with distinct reproduction
invariants: mutual dependence once established tends to persist (ratchet)
transformations: gene transfer from symbiont to host
conserved_quantities: the complementary function set of the holobiont (division of labour)
failure_modes: irreversible dependence on a degraded partner
memory: vertically transmitted symbiont carries lineage history
identity: holobiont vs separate individuals; the unit of selection is ambiguous
information: partners sense different aspects of the environment

unexplained: whether measure theory contributes mechanism or only vocabulary
which interpretation gives a prediction beyond threshold public goods
Measure Theory knockout is weak for M1, M2, M9, M12, M13; Compressed Sensing is weak for M3, M7, M11, M14
M12 critical dependence may reduce to cost accounting
L2 on finite spaces risks trivial absolute continuity
no lens yet separates steepness of the benefit from CS specifically
M4, M5, M6, M7, M8, M10, M11, M14 have no world yet
W1 may only confirm a known threshold public-goods effect

hypotheses.statement: Mutualism as crossing a joint recovery phase transition: host and symbiont each hold too few measurements of a shared sparse environment to decode it alone, but their stacked measurements exceed the threshold; the sharpness of the CS transition is what makes the partnership obligate.

Endosymbiotic genome reduction as Lebesgue decomposition: the symbiont's functional measure splits into a part absolutely continuous w.r.t. the host's (redundant, lost under cost) and a singular part (retained); the reduced symbiont is the singular remainder.

Symbiosis as exchange of sigma-algebras rather than of goods: each partner's sensors define a partition of environmental states; the holobiont acts on the join partition, and the currency of the partnership is resolvable events, not resources.

Complementarity as null-space transversality: what one partner cannot see (ker A_host) is what the other sees; selection on partnerships is selection for the joint null-space property of the stacked measurement matrix.

Cheating as aliasing: a cheater is a strategy lying in the same measurement coset (x + ker A) as a cooperator; the host's ability to sanction is bounded by the RIP/spark of its verification matrix, so cheater evolution is an attack on the host's sensing geometry.

Dependence dynamics as convergence theorems: the monotone ratchet of gene loss is monotone convergence; a host-imposed cap is a dominating function that makes the symbiont limit exist; lack of domination is escape of mass, i.e. the mutualism-to-parasitism blowout.

Critical dependence: gene transfer from symbiont to host proceeds until the host alone sits just below the recovery threshold, so endosymbioses are poised at a phase boundary where the symbiont's residual contribution is minimal but indispensable.

Free-rider stabilisation by a steep recovery curve: partners pool measurement rows to decode a k-sparse environment; because success collapses abruptly below m*(k), any partner that trims its rows sinks the pair, so the steepness of the CS phase transition polices free-riding.

concept_contributions.Compressed Sensing: steep, threshold-like benefit curve P(success | m, k)
concept_contributions.Measure Theory: success probability as the measure of the set of recovered signals/draws (concentration of measure makes it steep)
concept_contributions.Symbiosis: two lineages that pool contributions and can free-ride

knockouts.Compressed Sensing: benefit becomes smooth in m; free-riding erodes contributions gradually (tragedy of the commons)
knockouts.Measure Theory: weak: only the probabilistic reading of success; a deterministic threshold gives the same effect
knockouts.Symbiosis: no partners: reduces to single-agent budget optimisation

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: threshold public-goods game / volunteer's dilemma with an arbitrary step benefit

questions.what_exists: agents with heritable row budget m_i and a pooling bit
questions.what_is_selected: row budget and willingness to pool
questions.distinguishing_observable: pooled total m concentrates within +-15% of m*(k) under CS benefit but decays under a smooth benefit with matched mean

hypotheses.statement: Selection for transverse null spaces: pair-level selection acts on the joint null-space property of the stacked matrix [A_h; A_s], pushing partners' kernels apart so that no sparse vector is invisible to both.

concept_contributions.Compressed Sensing: null space / spark as the object of selection
concept_contributions.Measure Theory: kernel as a null set of the partner's measurement pushforward

knockouts.Compressed Sensing: nothing to be transverse; complementarity becomes resource-based only
knockouts.Measure Theory: weak: kernels are linear algebra; the null-set reading is interpretive
knockouts.Symbiosis: no pairing: each agent optimises its own matrix, cross-kernel angles random

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: classic coevolutionary complementarity / division of labour under vertical transmission

questions.what_exists: host and symbiont measurement row sets
questions.distinguishing_observable: cross-partner row redundancy and joint coherence lower under vertical than horizontal transmission with matched selection

hypotheses.statement: Singular-remainder genome reduction: under per-gene cost, the symbiont loses genes whose function lies in the support of the host's function measure; the retained genome converges to the part singular w.r.t. the host.

concept_contributions.Compressed Sensing: weak: enters only through the M13 variant where the host verifies via compressed checks
concept_contributions.Measure Theory: Lebesgue decomposition and monotone decrease of overlapping mass
concept_contributions.Symbiosis: endosymbiotic gene loss under host provisioning

knockouts.Compressed Sensing: weak - mechanism survives as plain redundancy loss
knockouts.Measure Theory: lose the prediction that overlap mass goes to ~0 rather than merely decreasing
knockouts.Symbiosis: no host support to be singular against

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: redundant genes are lost because they are costly and unneeded

questions.what_exists: symbiont gene-expression vector, host support set
questions.distinguishing_observable: overlap energy of the symbiont genome on host support falls below 5% while off-support required genes are retained

hypotheses.statement: Sigma-algebra exchange: partners exchange partitions (which events they can resolve) instead of estimates; the holobiont's policy must be measurable w.r.t. the join, and the partnership's value is the number of fitness-relevant events measurable only in the join.

concept_contributions.Compressed Sensing: each partition is induced by few quantised measurements of a sparse state
concept_contributions.Measure Theory: join of sigma-algebras; measurability of the policy
concept_contributions.Symbiosis: two partners whose partitions are coarse alone

knockouts.Compressed Sensing: partitions arbitrary; no reason joins are small or efficient
knockouts.Measure Theory: lose the event-level accounting; becomes feature concatenation
knockouts.Symbiosis: single agent with the union of sensors

questions.distinguishing_observable: the holobiont policy uses events outside each partner's sigma-algebra; the count of such events predicts benefit better than total bits exchanged

hypotheses.statement: Coset-bounded sanctions: a host rewards a symbiont on the basis of sparse recovery from its m verification measurements; cheaters evolve cheap contributions in the same measurement coset as expensive beneficial ones, and cheater success is governed by the host's verification geometry.

concept_contributions.Compressed Sensing: verification by m measurements; aliasing in ker A
concept_contributions.Measure Theory: coset x + ker A as the equivalence class 'equal as far as the host can measure'

knockouts.Compressed Sensing: host sees contributions fully: no aliasing, no cheaters

questions.what_exists: host verification matrix, symbiont contribution vectors
questions.what_persists: cheater lineages in ker A directions
questions.distinguishing_observable: exploitation gap (paid reward minus delivered benefit) vs host m shows a threshold near the L1 transition rather than a smooth decline

hypotheses.statement: Filtration carried by the partner: a vertically transmitted symbiont stores a compressed record (few rows) of the host lineage's environmental history; the lineage's sigma-algebra grows as a filtration across generations, while horizontal transmission resets it.

concept_contributions.Compressed Sensing: history stored as few measurements of a sparse environment history
concept_contributions.Measure Theory: filtration and martingale convergence of the lineage estimate

knockouts.Compressed Sensing: memory capacity scales with rows, not with k log(n/k)
knockouts.Symbiosis: memory held in host genome instead; no transmission-mode effect

questions.distinguishing_observable: memory capacity scales as m/log(n/k) environments under vertical transmission and collapses to one generation under horizontal

hypotheses.statement: Domination-bounded mutualism: the host imposes a dominating function (cap) on symbiont density; with an integrable cap the time-averaged holobiont fitness converges, without it symbiont mass escapes (sup grows, integrated benefit vanishes) - parasitism as failure of dominated convergence.

concept_contributions.Compressed Sensing: weak: host monitors symbiont density through compressed measurements; dependency is weak
concept_contributions.Measure Theory: dominated vs undominated convergence; escape of mass

knockouts.Compressed Sensing: weak - dynamics unchanged if the host measures density directly

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: logistic growth with a carrying capacity set by the host

questions.what_is_selected: caps that keep the limit integrable
questions.distinguishing_observable: mass outside a compact region diverges exactly when the cap is non-integrable, independent of mean cap level

hypotheses.statement: Holobiont as a sparse density ratio: symbiosis is the departure of the joint trait distribution from the product of marginals; if dP/d(P_h x P_s) is sparse in some basis, symbiosis is detectable from O(k log n) joint observations.

concept_contributions.Compressed Sensing: sparse recovery of the density ratio from few co-occurrence probes

knockouts.Compressed Sensing: sample complexity scales with ambient dimension

questions.what_exists: joint distribution of host and symbiont traits
questions.distinguishing_observable: detection sample complexity scales with sparsity of the density ratio, not with number of trait pairs

hypotheses.statement: Coherence minimisation as division of labour: a consortium with fixed total row budget evolves so that each member's rows are incoherent with the others', making mutual incoherence the emergent signature of specialisation.

concept_contributions.Compressed Sensing: mutual coherence of the stacked matrix governs recovery

questions.distinguishing_observable: joint column coherence falls below each member's own coherence more than under random re-pairing

hypotheses.statement: Dictionary-union symbiosis: partners carry different sparsifying dictionaries (e.g. spikes vs oscillations); signals sparse only in the union are decodable only by the holobiont, provided the dictionaries are mutually incoherent.

concept_contributions.Compressed Sensing: union-of-bases recovery and the uncertainty principle
concept_contributions.Measure Theory: support in the union as a decomposition of the signal

knockouts.Compressed Sensing: no representational advantage from the union
knockouts.Symbiosis: one agent holds the union dictionary

questions.what_is_selected: dictionaries whose union decodes the environment
questions.distinguishing_observable: recovery on mixed signals succeeds only when both partners are present and dictionaries are incoherent

hypotheses.statement: Cryptic variation in null sets: symbiont traits whose effects lie on environment events of measure zero are invisible to selection and drift; when the environment shifts to a measure not absolutely continuous w.r.t. the old one, this reservoir is exposed at once.

concept_contributions.Compressed Sensing: weak: only that kernel directions go unseen
concept_contributions.Measure Theory: absolute continuity of new vs old environment measure
concept_contributions.Symbiosis: symbiont as reservoir of hidden variation

knockouts.Measure Theory: lose the prediction that only non-a.c. shifts release variance
knockouts.Symbiosis: variation held in the host; mechanism is ordinary cryptic genetic variation

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: cryptic genetic variation released by environment change

questions.distinguishing_observable: fitness variance jump after a shift is large only for shifts with mass outside the old support

hypotheses.statement: Critical dependence under endosymbiotic row transfer: symbiont measurement rows migrate to the host; the symbiont, selected to shrink, and the host, sanctioning a dispensable partner, settle where the host alone sits just below m*(k) and the symbiont supplies the few rows that cross it.

concept_contributions.Compressed Sensing: the threshold m*(k) that defines 'just below'
concept_contributions.Measure Theory: monotone ratchet of transfer; loss is irreversible

knockouts.Compressed Sensing: no threshold: dependence ends at an arbitrary level set by costs
knockouts.Measure Theory: weak: the ratchet can be modelled without measure theory
knockouts.Symbiosis: no second level; host simply acquires rows

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: cost accounting: host keeps partner iff upkeep < cost of the rows it would need

questions.what_exists: holobionts with host rows and symbiont rows
questions.what_changes: row counts via transfer, gain, loss
questions.distinguishing_observable: retained-partner hosts cluster at m_h/m* in [0.6,1.0) under CS benefit but not under a smooth benefit with matched costs

hypotheses.statement: Verifiability-driven reduction: hosts sanction contributions they cannot explain from compressed checks in their own basis, so symbiont genomes become sparse in the host's basis rather than merely non-redundant.

concept_contributions.Compressed Sensing: host verifies via sparse recovery in its basis
concept_contributions.Measure Theory: weak: singular vs a.c. parts are not the driver

knockouts.Compressed Sensing: reduction direction arbitrary w.r.t. host basis

questions.what_exists: symbiont expression vectors, host basis and checks

hypotheses.statement: Singular coexistence: partners whose resource-use measures are mutually singular coexist without competition even when supports interleave densely (Cantor-like); interaction strength is the mass of the absolutely continuous overlap, not support proximity.

concept_contributions.Compressed Sensing: weak: only that singular supports can be sparse in a wavelet basis

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: niche differentiation measured by overlap indices

questions.distinguishing_observable: coexistence predicted by a.c.-overlap mass but not by a smoothed overlap index when supports are fractal and interleaved

lenses.name: Null-space cartography
lenses.rationale: Complementarity claims (I4) live in the geometry of kernels; this lens makes kernels first-class.
lenses.transformation: compute kernels, principal angles between kernels, empirical joint null-space constant by sampling sparse vectors
observables: min principal angle between ker A_h and ker A_s
fraction of random k-sparse vectors with ||[A_h;A_s]x|| < eps||x||
predictedSignals: angles rise and duplicates fall under vertical transmission
lenses.nullExpectation: random pairing gives angle and duplicate distributions of independent draws
failureModes: angles uninformative when m_h+m_s is near n
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: measures complementarity without reference to fitness

lenses.name: Radon-Nikodym ledger
lenses.rationale: Genome reduction and coexistence claims are about a.c. vs singular mass.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: partner function/resource profiles as measures on a finite function set
lenses.transformation: Lebesgue decomposition of the symbiont measure w.r.t. the host measure over time; RN derivative on the overlap
predictedSignals: a.c. mass fraction decays monotonically to <0.05 under M3
lenses.nullExpectation: a.c. fraction decays only in proportion to total genome loss
failureModes: on finite spaces every measure is a.c. w.r.t. counting measure; the host measure must be the reference
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: separates 'lost because redundant' from 'lost because costly'

lenses.name: Donoho-Tanner placement
lenses.rationale: Several mechanisms predict where populations sit relative to the recovery transition.
lenses.transformation: map each agent and pair to (delta=m/n, rho=k/m) and to distance from an empirically calibrated transition curve
observables: histogram of distances to the curve
predictedSignals: host alone just below, pair just above the curve (M12)
lenses.nullExpectation: distances spread without a mode at the curve
failureModes: transition curve calibrated with a different decoder than the agents use
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: reads population state in the native coordinates of compressed sensing

lenses.name: Sigma-algebra lattice
lenses.rationale: I3 claims the currency of the partnership is resolvable events.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: each partner's quantised sensor as a partition of environment states
lenses.transformation: compute join/meet, partition entropy, and which fitness-relevant events are measurable in each partner and in the join
observables: number of fitness events measurable only in the join
predictedSignals: benefit tracks join-only event count more than bits exchanged
failureModes: partition explosion in continuous state spaces

lenses.name: Cheater coset census
lenses.rationale: I5 frames cheaters as members of measurement cosets.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: symbiont contribution vectors and host verification matrix
lenses.transformation: project each contribution onto ker A and range(A^T); decompose into verified and unverified components
predictedSignals: cheater lineages accumulate mass in ker A
gap drops sharply near the L1 transition
failureModes: cost structure alone determines cheating; geometry irrelevant
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: locates cheating in the host's sensing geometry

lenses.name: Escape-of-mass tracker
lenses.rationale: I6 recasts parasitism as a convergence failure.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: time series of symbiont density profiles
lenses.transformation: compute tightness (mass outside compact K), sup vs integral, dominated-convergence checks
predictedSignals: non-integrable cap gives tightness failure preceding host collapse
lenses.nullExpectation: collapse predicted equally well by mean cap level
failureModes: finite simulations never show true escape
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: early-warning diagnostic distinct from mean density

lenses.name: Replicator frequency dynamics
lenses.rationale: Stock evolutionary lens to anchor strategy frequencies against the invented lenses.
predictedSignals: pooling stable only near the transition
lenses.nullExpectation: pooling frequency independent of benefit curvature

experiments.hypothesis: A steep (CS) benefit curve stabilises pooled measurement budgets against free-riding; a smooth benefit curve with matched mean does not.
experiments.mechanism: Agents carry heritable row budget m_i (0..60) and a pooling bit; random pairs; if both pool, success = P(m_1+m_2, k), else P(m_i, k); fitness = success - c*m_i.
experiments.intervention: benefit table P(m,k) estimated by OMP on Gaussian A (n=100, k=8, 40 trials per m, m=0..120)
experiments.control: same dynamics with the null-twin benefit table
experiments.positive_control: step benefit P = 1[m >= m*]; must give pooled total within +-15% of m*, else the world is uninformative
experiments.observable: final pooling frequency f_pool; mean pooled total T = mean(m_1+m_2) over pooling pairs; mean success
experiments.success_criterion: in >=8/10 seeds: f_pool >= 0.8 and |T/m* - 1| <= 0.15 in the CS arm, AND mean success(CS) - mean success(null) >= 0.3
experiments.failure_criterion: f_pool < 0.5 in the CS arm in >=5/10 seeds, OR success difference < 0.1
experiments.alternative_explanation: any convex-then-saturating benefit gives the same result; CS contributes nothing beyond steepness
experiments.null_twin: benefit table replaced by a monotone linear ramp between P(0) and P(120), rescaled to equal mean over m=0..120 (matches mean and endpoints, destroys the transition)
experiments.why_this_implementation: Wright-Fisher population with integer traits and a lookup benefit table; the claim is about selection on budgets, so no learning system is needed. Displaced alternative: multi-agent RL, which would add credit-assignment confounds.
experiments.size: n=100, k=8, 100 agents, 500 generations, mutation m +-1 at 0.05, pooling flip 0.01, c=0.005, 10 seeds x 3 arms
stupid_explanations: mutation bias toward lower m drives free-riding in both arms
m* sits near the max budget so the cap does the work
the linear null has lower marginal return near m*, so selection intensity differs

experiments.hypothesis: With row transfer, symbiont-level shrinkage and host sanctions, retained-symbiont holobionts cluster with the host alone just below threshold (m_h/m* in [0.6,1.0)) under CS benefit but not under a smooth benefit.
experiments.mechanism: Holobiont = host rows H (m_h) + symbiont rows S (m_s), Gaussian, n=64, k=4. Per generation: success s = OMP recovery rate on 4 fresh k-sparse signals from [H;S]; host tests H alone and expels S if alone-success >= 0.75. Host fitness = s - c_h*m_h - c_u*1[S retained]. Mutations: host gain/lose row p=0.05 each, transfer S->H p=0.02, symbiont loses a row p=0.1 (proxy for within-host selection for smaller symbionts).
experiments.positive_control: success = step 1[m_h+m_s >= m*]; must give F_crit >= 0.7, else the world is uninformative
experiments.observable: F_crit = fraction of final holobionts with S retained and m_h/m* in [0.6,1.0); IQR of m_h/m*
experiments.success_criterion: CS arm F_crit >= 0.5 in >=3/4 seeds for at least 2 of 3 c_u values, AND null twin F_crit <= 0.2 at the same c_u values
experiments.failure_criterion: CS arm F_crit < 0.3 at all c_u, OR null twin F_crit >= 0.4 (clustering from cost structure, not the transition)
experiments.alternative_explanation: host keeps the partner purely because c_u < c_h * rows_needed; clustering near m* is an artefact of initial conditions
experiments.null_twin: success = 1 - normalised error of min-norm least squares on dense Gaussian signals (about m/n), costs rescaled so initial mean fitness matches the CS arm; keeps transfer/sanction dynamics, destroys the phase transition
experiments.why_this_implementation: Explicit two-level evolutionary simulation with a linear-algebra fitness oracle; the phenomenon concerns row counts relative to a threshold, so no neural or RL component is warranted.
experiments.size: n=64, k=4, 30 holobionts, 200 generations, 4 test signals per eval, 3 c_u values x 3 arms (CS, null, positive control) x 4 seeds = 36 runs
stupid_explanations: initial m_h already near 0.8 m* and dynamics too slow to move it
the 0.75 expulsion threshold itself defines the band
OMP noise with 4 test signals makes success near threshold random, retaining partners by chance

experiments.hypothesis: Vertical (pair-level) transmission drives host and symbiont to hold complementary, non-redundant measurement rows, raising joint recovery beyond horizontal transmission with matched selection.
experiments.mechanism: Fixed palette of 64 candidate rows over n=32 (32 Hadamard rows + 32 random sparse +-1 rows with 4 nonzeros); each partner holds 8 palette indices; pair success = OMP recovery rate for k=3 signals from the 16 stacked rows; mutation replaces one index (p=0.1 per partner).
experiments.intervention: vertical arm: pairs reproduce as units under tournament selection on pair success
experiments.control: horizontal arm: identical selection on pair success, but offspring hosts and symbionts re-paired at random each generation
experiments.positive_control: hand-built pair with disjoint Hadamard halves must reach success >= 0.9; random-pair baseline recorded
experiments.observable: R = mean fraction of symbiont indices duplicated in the host; mean pair success; stacked column coherence
experiments.success_criterion: in >=8/10 seeds: R(vertical) <= 0.5 * R(horizontal) AND success(vertical) - success(horizontal) >= 0.15
experiments.failure_criterion: R ratio > 0.8 or success difference < 0.05 in >=5/10 seeds
experiments.alternative_explanation: vertical transmission simply raises heritability of pair fitness; any additive complementarity would show this
experiments.null_twin: horizontal arm: same mutation, selection intensity and palette, pairing randomised each generation, destroying partner-specific complementarity
experiments.why_this_implementation: A discrete palette makes redundancy exactly countable and OMP recovery is the fitness oracle. Graph or neural encodings would obscure the kernel geometry that L1 measures.
experiments.size: n=32, k=3, 50 pairs, 300 generations, 6 test signals, 10 seeds x 2 arms
stupid_explanations: the horizontal arm has lower effective selection so everything is worse there
duplicates are purged in the vertical arm simply because they are wasted rows, independent of kernels
Hadamard rows are near-optimal so any selection converges on them

experiments.hypothesis: Sanctions based on compressed verification in the host's basis make symbiont genomes sparse in that basis beyond what matched random sanctions produce; redundancy loss alone drives host-overlap mass to ~0 in both arms.
experiments.mechanism: n=64 functions; required set R (|R|=24); host support S_h (12 of R); symbiont expression w in R^64 starts at 0.5 everywhere. Benefit = sum over R of min(host_i + w_i, 1)/24; cost 0.01*||w||_1. Sanction arm: host takes 24 measurements y = A Psi_h^T w (Psi_h random orthonormal), recovers 6-sparse Psi_h coefficients by OMP, sanction probability = unexplained energy fraction.
experiments.control: random sanctions with per-generation rate matched to the sanction arm
experiments.positive_control: a symbiont initialised 6-sparse in Psi_h must incur a sanction rate < 0.05
experiments.observable: s_Psi = number of Psi_h coefficients holding 90% of ||w||^2; overlap fraction = ||w on S_h||^2 / ||w||^2
experiments.success_criterion: M13: s_Psi(sanction) <= 0.7 * s_Psi(null) in >=8/10 seeds. M3: overlap fraction <= 0.05 in both arms in >=8/10 seeds
experiments.failure_criterion: M13 fails if the s_Psi ratio > 0.9 in >=5/10 seeds; M3 fails if the overlap fraction > 0.2 in >=5/10 seeds
experiments.alternative_explanation: sanctions just shrink ||w|| overall, which lowers s_Psi via thresholding noise
experiments.null_twin: random sanctions at matched rate: same sanction magnitude, no dependence on legibility in Psi_h
experiments.why_this_implementation: Mutation-selection hill-climbing over expression vectors (population of 60) is the minimal setting in which a verification matrix can shape genome direction; no learned model is needed.
experiments.size: n=64, m=24 checks, 60 symbionts, 400 generations, 10 seeds x 2 arms
stupid_explanations: s_Psi falls because w shrinks toward zero
benefit saturation makes many genome directions neutral so any pressure picks one
a random orthonormal Psi_h makes canonical sparse vectors dense, so the tension is built in by construction
